 Candidates for Fresno County Superintendent of Schools share their strategies ahead of election day 
 Fresno County voters are choosing who will guide the future of more than 30 school districts and the students they serve. KFSN By Kerry Mannix Tuesday, November 3, 2026 2:26AM Share FRESNO COUNTY, Calif. (KFSN) -- Fresno County voters are choosing who will guide the future of more than 30 school districts and the students they serve.
 The Superintendent of Schools race is down to two candidates.
 The incumbent, Michele Cantwell-Copher, has held the position since January of 2023.
 Challenging her is former Clovis Unified Superintendent Eimear O'Brien.
 The winner will lead the way when it comes to overseeing district finances, ensuring state requirements are met and providing support to schools and educators.
 Both candidates have decades of education experience, and both want to foster greater student success.
 But they have different strategies for achieving that.
 As student achievement remains a major concern, both candidates say improving academic outcomes is a priority.
 "The literacy crisis has been the centerpiece of my campaign," said O'Brien. "There are many schools and classrooms in Fresno County using the science of reading, but we need to scale it up as a county."
 "The experiences for each of our students across different school sites can be very, very, vastly different. But there are some common practices and instruction and programs that yield better results. And so, my job has been to sort of harness all of the best practices," said Cantwell-Copher.
 But improving student performance also takes resources and making sure taxpayer dollars are spent responsibly.

 "I want us to take a hard look at the programs we're using the money for. I've seen what it looks like when the money is used to train... not just to train teachers -- train administrators who are there to support and evaluate teachers," said O'Brien.
 "I'm well aware of the current and the future fiscal challenges. I think about those less so in terms of budgeting for schools -- because frankly, I do that well -- but more so about what those conditions might look like in our families, and does that mean more students will come to school hungry?" said Cantwell-Copher. "Today, we have to think intentionally about providing so that our students can do their job of learning in our schools."
 While both candidates say collaboration is critical, they have different ideas about how the county office can best support local schools.
 From working with district leaders to engaging parents and community partners, each says their approach can make an impact.
 Voters have until 8 p.m. Tuesday to cast their ballots.
